title: In Korean, a fish is 'water meat' 🐟 물고기 #learnkorean
caption:
물 (mul) means water. Korean builds a lot of words just by adding them up:

물 + 고기 (meat) = 물고기 — fish
눈 (eye) + 물 = 눈물 — tears
물 + 개 (dog) = 물개 — seal

Say them with me: mul-go-gi, nun-mul, mul-gae.

pinnedComment: Guess this one: 눈 + 사람 (person) = ? Hint: it is not 'eye person' 👀
alt: A needle-felted cafe counter. A marbled felt steak drops into a round glass fishbowl with a splash. Word cards read 물 water and 고기 meat, and the steak starts swimming: 물고기, water meat? The coral felt mascot gasps "My lunch!!" A real orange goldfish swims up and stares at the steak: 물고기, FISH. The mascot cries over an empty plate; the camera moves to its eye, 눈, and a tear, 물: 눈물, TEARS. A felt puppy leaps into the bowl and paddles: 물개, water dog? The water bursts and a grey felt seal rises with the steak balanced on its nose: 물개, SEAL. The mascot bounces with joy. Last line: Just add 물.
